newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack to speed up crash claims process.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack to speed up crash claims process.

text.p: Railtrack Plc, the rail infrastructure operator privatised last year, promised to accelerate efforts to deal with compensation claims from rail crash victims on Thursday.

Sir Robert Horton, chairman, made the promise at the annual general meeting (AGM) in London after coming under attack from passenger pressure Group Save Our Railways (SOR) and Railtrack's own shareholders.

Morton said he would respond to a recent letter from UK transport minister Glenda Jackson who has expressed concern about the lack of progress in dealing with claims, referring to the crash at Stafford in particular.

The annual meeting saw a spate of criticism from investors. Keith Bill, spokesman for SOR, told the AGM that Railtrack had obstructed claims from victims of three rail crashes at Stafford, Bexley and Watford.

"Every conceivable obstacle has been put in the way of achieving the truth about these crashes," he said. But Railtrack denied it had slowed down the claims process. It said the compensation process was not its responsibility.
In an earlier statement, the company rebuffed SOR's claims that "profits are consistently put before the public interest."
The company replied "Railtrack has and will always maintain that rail safety is the top priority but these are not just empty words."
But there were few other disruptions to the group's second AGM since its flotation in May 1996.
Railtrack's shares marked the occasion by hitting an all-time high of 800 pence, rising 15 pence per share.
The group's shares have steadied in recent sessions after the company backed away from a possible confrontation with the Office of the Rail Regulator.

The group agreed to a Rail Regulator John Swift's demands for a change to its license conditions, avoiding uncertainty over its future and the risk of deteriorating relations with the regulator and the new Labour government.
On Tuesday Railtrack and Swift agreed the form of the license change. This will now undergo a period of consultation before it is published.
